/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — `CombinatorialCech`

The constant-coefficient combinatorial core of standard-cover Čech acyclicity
(planner step **L3**, `analogies/p3-localisation.md`).  After localising the
extended Čech complex at a spanning element `s_r` (planner step L2, via
`exact_of_isLocalized_span`), the fixed index `r` becomes globally available, and
the alternating Čech coboundary admits the explicit contracting homotopy
`h(t)_{i₀…i_p} = t_{r i₀…i_p}` of Stacks
`lemma-cech-cohomology-quasi-coherent-trivial`.

This section formalises that homotopy and its consequences for the **constant
coefficient** complex `Cᵖ = (Fin (p+1) → ι) → M` with alternating coface
differential — abstracted away from the localisation/geometry so the purely
combinatorial cancellation (`combHomotopy`) and the simplicial identity
(`combDifferential_comp`, `d² = 0`) are isolated and reusable.  The remaining
work to close `CechAcyclic.affine` is the **L1** categorical bridge identifying
the abstract `CechComplex` terms with the away-localisation modules `M_{s_σ}` and
its differential with this `combDifferential` (after localising at `s_r`); these
lemmas are then fed to `exact_of_isLocalized_span` node by node.

These declarations are `private`: they exist only to close `CechAcyclic.affine`
in this file.  The intended blueprint home is the `\lean{...}` bundle of
`lem:cech_acyclic_affine`. -/

namespace CombinatorialCech

variable {ι : Type*} {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] {n : ℕ}

/-- Alternating coface (Čech) differential with constant coefficients in `M`:
`Cⁿ = (Fin n → ι) → M ⟶ Cⁿ⁺¹`, `(d t)(σ) = ∑ⱼ (-1)ʲ • t (σ ∘ j.succAbove)`.
The argument `σ ∘ j.succAbove` is the `(n)`-tuple obtained from the `(n+1)`-tuple
`σ` by deleting the `j`-th index. -/
private def combDifferential (t : (Fin n → ι) → M) : (Fin (n + 1) → ι) → M :=
  fun σ => ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) • t (σ ∘ j.succAbove)

/-- The contracting homotopy of the localised complex: prepend the fixed
(globally invertible after localising at `s_r`) index `r`.
`(h u)(τ) = u (Fin.cons r τ)`. -/
private def combHomotopy (r : ι) (u : (Fin (n + 1) → ι) → M) : (Fin n → ι) → M :=
  fun τ => u (Fin.cons r τ)

@[simp] private lemma combHomotopy_zero (r : ι) :
    combHomotopy (M := M) (n := n) r 0 = 0 := by
  funext τ; simp [combHomotopy]

/-- Composing `Fin.cons r` with the `(j+1)`-th coface map is `Fin.cons r` of the
`j`-th coface map: the bookkeeping identity behind the homotopy computation. -/
lemma cons_comp_succAbove_succ (r : ι) (σ : Fin (n + 1) → ι) (k : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (Fin.cons r σ : Fin (n + 2) → ι) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove
      = Fin.cons r (σ ∘ k.succAbove) := by
  funext l
  refine Fin.cases ?_ ?_ l
  · simp

1509	  Concrete.productEquiv
1510	    (fun σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι => F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k))))
1511

1513	underlying group map of the categorical projection `Pi.π … σ`.  A definitional
1514	restatement of `Concrete.productEquiv_apply_apply`, named so that downstream proofs can
1515	`rw` it without fighting the `Concrete.productEquiv` coercion. -/

1517	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (p : ℕ)
1518	    (y : ToType ((sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk p)))
1519	    (σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι) :
1520	    sectionCechProductEquiv U F p y σ
1521	      = ConcreteCategory.hom
1522	          (Pi.π (fun σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι => F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) σ) y :=
1523	  Concrete.productEquiv_apply_apply _ y σ

1528	`objD q`, `objD (q+1)` form an exact sequence.  Pure homological algebra: combines
1529	`exactAt_iff_isZero_homology`, `exactAt_iff'`, and the abelian-group exactness
1530	criterion `ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact`. -/

1532	    (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (q : ℕ)
1533	    (h : Function.Exact
1534	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) q))
1535	      (ConcreteCategory.hom
1536	        (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) (q + 1)))) :
1537	    IsZero ((sectionCechComplex U F).homology (q + 1)) := by
1538	  rw [← HomologicalComplex.exactAt_iff_isZero_homology,
1539	      (sectionCechComplex U F).exactAt_iff' q (q + 1) (q + 2) (by simp) (by simp),
1540	      ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact]
1541	  have hf : (sectionCechComplex U F).d q (q + 1)
1542	      = AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) q :=
1543	    CochainComplex.of_d (fun n => (sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk n))
1544	      (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F)) q
1545	  have hg : (sectionCechComplex U F).d (q + 1) (q + 2)
1546	      = AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) (q + 1) :=
1547	    CochainComplex.of_d (fun n => (sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk n))
1548	      (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F)) (q + 1)
1549	  change Function.Exact
1550	      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((sectionCechComplex U F).d q (q + 1)))
1551	      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((sectionCechComplex U F).d (q + 1) (q + 2)))
1552	  rw [hf, hg]
1553	  exact h
1554	
1555	/-- Application of a finite sum of `Ab`-morphisms distributes over the sum. -/
1556	private lemma ab_hom_finsetSum_apply {A B : Ab.{u}} {κ : Type*}
1557	    (s : Finset κ) (f : κ → (A ⟶ B)) (t : ToType A) :
1558	    ConcreteCategory.hom (∑ i ∈ s, f i) t = ∑ i ∈ s, ConcreteCategory.hom (f i) t := by
1559	  classical
1560	  induction s using Finset.induction with
1561	  | empty => simp
1562	  | insert a s ha ih =>
1563	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha, AddCommGrpCat.hom_add_apply, ih]
1564	
1565	/-- The `i`-th section {\v C}ech face restriction at a multi-index `σ` of the
1566	cosimplicial section object: the presheaf restriction of `F` from the deleted-face
1567	intersection `⨅ₗ U (σ (δ i l))` to the full intersection `⨅ₖ U (σ k)`.  Factored as a
1568	named `def` so the cosimplicial differential (`sectionCech_objD_apply`) refers to it
1569	by name rather than re-elaborating the `homOfLE (le_iInf …)` term. -/
1570	noncomputable def sectionCechFaceRestr {ι : Type u} (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
1571	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) {q : ℕ} (σ : Fin (q + 2) → ι) (i : Fin (q + 2)) :
1572	    F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ l, U ((σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom) l)))
1573	      ⟶ F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k))) :=
1574	  F.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_iInf
1575	    (fun l => iInf_le _ ((SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom l)))).op
1576	
1577	/-- **(c2, abstract) Coface match**: the underlying group action of the section
1578	{\v C}ech coface differential `objD q`, read through the product equivalence, is the
1579	alternating sum of the presheaf restriction maps applied to the deleted-face
1580	coordinates — exactly the shape of `SectionCechModule.dDiff`.  This is purely about
1581	the cosimplicial structure of `sectionCechCosimplicial`; no sheaf identification yet. -/
1582	lemma sectionCech_objD_apply {ι : Type u} (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
1583	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (q : ℕ)
1584	    (t : ToType ((sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk q)))
1585	    (σ : Fin (q + 2) → ι) :

1587	        (ConcreteCategory.hom
1588	          (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) q) t) σ
1589	      = ∑ i : Fin (q + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) •
1590	          ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U F σ i)
1591	            (sectionCechProductEquiv U F q t (σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom)) := by

1598	          = ConcreteCategory.hom
1599	              (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) q
1600	                ≫ Pi.π (fun σ : Fin (q + 2) → ι => F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) σ) t

/-!
# Ext groups in abelian categories

Let `C` be an abelian category (with `C : Type u` and `Category.{v} C`).
In this file, we introduce the assumption `HasExt.{w} C` which asserts
that morphisms between single complexes in arbitrary degrees in
the derived category of `C` are `w`-small. Under this assumption,
we define `Ext.{w} X Y n : Type w` as shrunk versions of suitable
types of morphisms in the derived category. In particular, when `C` has
enough projectives or enough injectives, the property `HasExt.{v} C`
shall hold.

Note: in certain situations, `w := v` shall be the preferred
choice of universe (e.g. if `C := ModuleCat.{v} R` with `R : Type v`).
However, in the development of the API for Ext-groups, it is important
to keep a larger degree of generality for universes, as `w < v`
may happen in certain situations. Indeed, if `X : Scheme.{u}`,
then the underlying category of the étale site of `X` shall be a large
category. However, the category `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`
shall have good properties (because there is a small category of affine
schemes with the same category of sheaves), and even though the type of
morphisms in `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}` shall be
in `Type (u + 1)`, these types are going to be `u`-small.
Then, for `C := Sheaf X.etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, we will have
`Category.{u + 1} C`, but `HasExt.{u} C` will hold
(as `C` has enough injectives). Then, the `Ext` groups between étale
sheaves over `X` shall be in `Type u`.

-/

216	theorem injective_toPresheafOfModules (I : X.Modules) [Injective I] :

252	`Hom(free(yoneda V), F) ≃ F(V)` is evaluation of the morphism's component at `V` on the

256	lemma freeYonedaHomEquiv_apply (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.PresheafOfModules)

258	    freeYonedaHomEquiv V F ψ
259	      = (ConcreteCategory.hom (ψ.app (Opposite.op V))) (ModuleCat.freeMk (𝟙 V)) := by
260	  simp only [freeYonedaHomEquiv]; rfl

260	  simp only [freeYonedaHomEquiv]; rfl

262	/-- **Additive upgrade of `freeYonedaHomEquiv`.** The free–Yoneda hom bijection
263	`Hom_{PMod}(free(yoneda V), F) ≃ F(V)` is an isomorphism of abelian groups: the source is

274	noncomputable def freeYonedaHomAddEquiv (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)

281	  right_inv := (freeYonedaHomEquiv V F).right_inv

307	    Pi.π _ (σ ∘ f.toOrderHom) ≫
308	      F.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_iInf (fun l => iInf_le _ (f.toOrderHom l)))).op)

310	    -- The map at `𝟙 n` projects to index `σ ∘ id = σ` and restricts along the thin
311	    -- (reflexive) `Opens` hom `homOfLE ⋯ : ⨅ U(σ k) ⟶ ⨅ U(σ k)`, which is the identity.

313	    simp only [Pi.lift_π]
314	    -- the restriction hom is an endomorphism in the thin `Opensᵒᵖ` category, hence `𝟙`

316	    -- `erw` is needed: the `Subsingleton.elim` rewrite leaves the term not type-correct

318	    erw [CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, Category.comp_id]

320	    apply Pi.hom_ext
321	    intro σ
322	    simp only [Pi.lift_π, Category.assoc, SimplexCategory.comp_toOrderHom, OrderHom.comp_coe]
323	    rw [← Category.assoc, Pi.lift_π, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp]
324	    congr 1

330	`∏_{σ : Fin (p+1) → ι} F(⨅ₖ U (σ k))` and the alternating-sum-of-restrictions differential,

/-!
# Ext groups in abelian categories

Let `C` be an abelian category (with `C : Type u` and `Category.{v} C`).
In this file, we introduce the assumption `HasExt.{w} C` which asserts
that morphisms between single complexes in arbitrary degrees in
the derived category of `C` are `w`-small. Under this assumption,
we define `Ext.{w} X Y n : Type w` as shrunk versions of suitable
types of morphisms in the derived category. In particular, when `C` has
enough projectives or enough injectives, the property `HasExt.{v} C`
shall hold.

Note: in certain situations, `w := v` shall be the preferred
choice of universe (e.g. if `C := ModuleCat.{v} R` with `R : Type v`).
However, in the development of the API for Ext-groups, it is important
to keep a larger degree of generality for universes, as `w < v`
may happen in certain situations. Indeed, if `X : Scheme.{u}`,
then the underlying category of the étale site of `X` shall be a large
category. However, the category `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`
shall have good properties (because there is a small category of affine
schemes with the same category of sheaves), and even though the type of
morphisms in `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}` shall be
in `Type (u + 1)`, these types are going to be `u`-small.
Then, for `C := Sheaf X.etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, we will have
`Category.{u + 1} C`, but `HasExt.{u} C` will hold
(as `C` has enough injectives). Then, the `Ext` groups between étale
sheaves over `X` shall be in `Type u`.

-/

/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — `CombinatorialCech`

The constant-coefficient combinatorial core of standard-cover Čech acyclicity
(planner step **L3**, `analogies/p3-localisation.md`).  After localising the
extended Čech complex at a spanning element `s_r` (planner step L2, via
`exact_of_isLocalized_span`), the fixed index `r` becomes globally available, and
the alternating Čech coboundary admits the explicit contracting homotopy
`h(t)_{i₀…i_p} = t_{r i₀…i_p}` of Stacks
`lemma-cech-cohomology-quasi-coherent-trivial`.

This section formalises that homotopy and its consequences for the **constant
coefficient** complex `Cᵖ = (Fin (p+1) → ι) → M` with alternating coface
differential — abstracted away from the localisation/geometry so the purely
combinatorial cancellation (`combHomotopy`) and the simplicial identity
(`combDifferential_comp`, `d² = 0`) are isolated and reusable.  The remaining
work to close `CechAcyclic.affine` is the **L1** categorical bridge identifying
the abstract `CechComplex` terms with the away-localisation modules `M_{s_σ}` and
its differential with this `combDifferential` (after localising at `s_r`); these
lemmas are then fed to `exact_of_isLocalized_span` node by node.

These declarations are `private`: they exist only to close `CechAcyclic.affine`
in this file.  The intended blueprint home is the `\lean{...}` bundle of
`lem:cech_acyclic_affine`. -/

namespace CombinatorialCech

variable {ι : Type*} {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] {n : ℕ}

/-- Alternating coface (Čech) differential with constant coefficients in `M`:
`Cⁿ = (Fin n → ι) → M ⟶ Cⁿ⁺¹`, `(d t)(σ) = ∑ⱼ (-1)ʲ • t (σ ∘ j.succAbove)`.
The argument `σ ∘ j.succAbove` is the `(n)`-tuple obtained from the `(n+1)`-tuple
`σ` by deleting the `j`-th index. -/
private def combDifferential (t : (Fin n → ι) → M) : (Fin (n + 1) → ι) → M :=
  fun σ => ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) • t (σ ∘ j.succAbove)

/-- The contracting homotopy of the localised complex: prepend the fixed
(globally invertible after localising at `s_r`) index `r`.
`(h u)(τ) = u (Fin.cons r τ)`. -/
private def combHomotopy (r : ι) (u : (Fin (n + 1) → ι) → M) : (Fin n → ι) → M :=
  fun τ => u (Fin.cons r τ)

@[simp] private lemma combHomotopy_zero (r : ι) :
    combHomotopy (M := M) (n := n) r 0 = 0 := by
  funext τ; simp [combHomotopy]

/-- Composing `Fin.cons r` with the `(j+1)`-th coface map is `Fin.cons r` of the
`j`-th coface map: the bookkeeping identity behind the homotopy computation. -/
lemma cons_comp_succAbove_succ (r : ι) (σ : Fin (n + 1) → ι) (k : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (Fin.cons r σ : Fin (n + 2) → ι) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove
      = Fin.cons r (σ ∘ k.succAbove) := by
  funext l
  refine Fin.cases ?_ ?_ l
  · simp

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.FullyFaithful
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallShiftedHom

/-!
# Ext groups in abelian categories

Let `C` be an abelian category (with `C : Type u` and `Category.{v} C`).
In this file, we introduce the assumption `HasExt.{w} C` which asserts
that morphisms between single complexes in arbitrary degrees in
the derived category of `C` are `w`-small. Under this assumption,
we define `Ext.{w} X Y n : Type w` as shrunk versions of suitable
types of morphisms in the derived category. In particular, when `C` has
enough projectives or enough injectives, the property `HasExt.{v} C`
shall hold.

Note: in certain situations, `w := v` shall be the preferred
choice of universe (e.g. if `C := ModuleCat.{v} R` with `R : Type v`).
However, in the development of the API for Ext-groups, it is important
to keep a larger degree of generality for universes, as `w < v`
may happen in certain situations. Indeed, if `X : Scheme.{u}`,
then the underlying category of the étale site of `X` shall be a large
category. However, the category `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`
shall have good properties (because there is a small category of affine
schemes with the same category of sheaves), and even though the type of
morphisms in `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}` shall be
in `Type (u + 1)`, these types are going to be `u`-small.
Then, for `C := Sheaf X.etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, we will have
`Category.{u + 1} C`, but `HasExt.{u} C` will hold
(as `C` has enough injectives). Then, the `Ext` groups between étale
sheaves over `X` shall be in `Type u`.

-/

**1. `injective_cech_acyclic` (`CechBridge.lean:874`, base-case ingredient of L3/via `BasisCovSystem.injective_acyclic`).**

2. Show the augmentation `K(U)_• → O_U[0]` (`O_U` = "presheaf that is `⊕_{i:V_i⊇V} k`-ish structure of the cover", concretely `coverStructurePresheaf`-analogue) is a quasi-iso, via the *sectionwise* contracting homotopy: fix `i_fix` with `V ⊆ U_{i_fix}`, homotopy `h(s)_{i₀,…,iₚ} = [i₀ = i_fix]·s_{i₁,…,iₚ}`, check `dh+hd=id` (`combHomotopy_spec`/`combDifferential_exact`, `FreePresheafComplex.lean:483-580`, coefficient-agnostic, ports verbatim).
3. Show `(sheafToPresheaf J _).obj I` is injective in the presheaf category, for `I` injective in `𝒮` — **one-liner** via `Injective.injective_of_adjoint (sheafificationAdjunction J (ModuleCat k)) I`, using Mathlib's free `PreservesFiniteLimits (presheafToSheaf J A)` instance (§C.4) — this step is **much shorter** than the `X.Modules` analogue `injective_toPresheafOfModules`.
4. `Hom(-,I_pshf)` is exact (`preadditiveYoneda_obj_preservesFiniteColimits_of_injective`, `CechBridge.lean:401`, category-generic, reuse verbatim).
5. Apply `Hom(-,I_pshf)` to the quasi-iso augmentation ⟹ quasi-iso of `Hom`-complexes; identify `Hom(K(U)_•,I_pshf)` with the section Čech complex `Č•(U,I)` (analogue of `cechComplex_hom_identification`/`homCechComplexMapOpIso`) — this identification against Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor` cosimplicial object (rather than a hand-rolled one) is genuinely new plumbing (~150-250 LOC) but structurally the same shape as `CechBridge.lean:121-369`.
6. Conclude: source complex is `Hom(-,I)` of a degree-0-concentrated complex ⟹ zero in positive degree ⟹ transport across the quasi-iso to `Č•(U,I)`'s positive-degree homology (exact tail of `CechBridge.lean:874-911`, structurally verbatim).

**2. `ses_cech_h1` (`CechBridge.lean:659-826`, L1's surjectivity ingredient — Stacks `lemma-ses-cech-h1`).**
Proof strategy (10 lines): given SES `0→F→G→H→0` and local lifts `sLoc i ∈ G(Uᵢ)` of `s∈H(⨆Uᵢ)`, form the degree-1 cochain of pairwise differences `dGcoord σ = sLoc(σ1)|_σ - sLoc(σ0)|_σ`; show `gπ` kills it (LES exactness on sections, from `hπι`/`hker`); lift the killed cochain into `F` pointwise (`hker`); show the lift is a genuine 1-cocycle in `F` (transport the `d²=0` identity of `G`'s cochain through the mono `fι`); apply `Ȟ¹(U,F)=0` to extract a 0-cochain `t` with `dt` = the lift (`sectionCech_one_coboundary_of_isZero_homology`); correct `sLoc` by `fι(t)` to get a genuinely compatible family; glue via `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSheafUniqueGluing` on `G`; check the glued section maps to `s` by separatedness of `H`. **Port cost**: mechanical (swap `X.PresheafOfModules`/its restriction API for `𝒮`'s `sheafToPresheaf`/`forget₂`-composed presheaf and Mathlib's generic sheaf-gluing lemma), but the sheer bookkeeping volume (7 private helper lemmas, `CechBridge.lean:552-635`) means this is a **large, low-conceptual-risk, high-LOC** port item — budget ~250-350 LOC.

**3. The Čech-hom-identification `cechComplex_hom_identification`/`homCechComplexMapOpIso`/`sectionCechComplexMapOpIso` (`CechBridge.lean:121-369`).**
This is the piece with the **least direct Mathlib precedent for the new setting**, because it must reconcile two different presentations of "the Čech complex": (a) Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor`'s `FormalCoproduct`-based cosimplicial object (used to define `Scheme.cechCochain`/`Scheme.cechCohomology`, `Carriers.lean:562-578`, the target the whole port must land on) versus (b) the free-presheaf-resolution's own natural cosimplicial presentation `Hom(K(U)_•,F)` (built from `Sigma.ι`/`opCoproductIsoProduct`/`piComparison`, mirroring `homCechSectionIsoApp`, `CechBridge.lean:162-254`). The `X.Modules` proof needed this because `sectionCechComplex` was **hand-rolled** to match `K(𝒰)_•`'s shape by construction; in the port, the target complex `Scheme.cechCochain` is fixed externally by `cechComplexFunctor`, so the identification must instead show `Hom(K(U)_•, F) ≅ (cechComplexFunctor U).obj (sheafToPresheaf.obj F)` degreewise (`Hom(⊕_σ free(yoneda V_σ), F) ≅ ∏_σ F(V_σ)`, matching `FormalCoproduct.mk _ U`.cech's degree-`p` object `U.power (Fin(p+1))`), then check differential-intertwining against `FormalCoproduct`'s coface maps rather than the project's own `homOfLE`-based ones. Budget ~150-250 LOC of genuinely new work; recommend prototyping the degree-0 and degree-1 cases by hand first (`lean_multi_attempt`/`lean_goal` against `FormalCoproduct.mk`'s unfolding) before committing to the general-`n` proof, since the `FormalCoproduct`/`SimplicialObject` API's defeq behavior around `U.power`/`E.rightOp` is unfamiliar territory for this codebase (no prior project usage found).

/-!
# Ext groups in abelian categories

Let `C` be an abelian category (with `C : Type u` and `Category.{v} C`).
In this file, we introduce the assumption `HasExt.{w} C` which asserts
that morphisms between single complexes in arbitrary degrees in
the derived category of `C` are `w`-small. Under this assumption,
we define `Ext.{w} X Y n : Type w` as shrunk versions of suitable
types of morphisms in the derived category. In particular, when `C` has
enough projectives or enough injectives, the property `HasExt.{v} C`
shall hold.

Note: in certain situations, `w := v` shall be the preferred
choice of universe (e.g. if `C := ModuleCat.{v} R` with `R : Type v`).
However, in the development of the API for Ext-groups, it is important
to keep a larger degree of generality for universes, as `w < v`
may happen in certain situations. Indeed, if `X : Scheme.{u}`,
then the underlying category of the étale site of `X` shall be a large
category. However, the category `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`
shall have good properties (because there is a small category of affine
schemes with the same category of sheaves), and even though the type of
morphisms in `Sheaf X.Etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}` shall be
in `Type (u + 1)`, these types are going to be `u`-small.
Then, for `C := Sheaf X.etale AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, we will have
`Category.{u + 1} C`, but `HasExt.{u} C` will hold
(as `C` has enough injectives). Then, the `Ext` groups between étale
sheaves over `X` shall be in `Type u`.

-/

3. 4. `Hom(-,I_pshf)` is exact (`preadditiveYoneda_obj_preservesFiniteColimits_of_injective`, `CechBridge.lean:401`, category-generic, reuse verbatim).
5. Apply `Hom(-,I_pshf)` to the quasi-iso augmentation ⟹ quasi-iso of `Hom`-complexes; identify `Hom(K(U)_•,I_pshf)` with the section Čech complex `Č•(U,I)` (analogue of `cechComplex_hom_identification`/`homCechComplexMapOpIso`) — this identification against Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor` cosimplicial object (rather than a hand-rolled one) is genuinely new plumbing (~150-250 LOC) but structurally the same shape as `CechBridge.lean:121-369`.
6. Conclude: source complex is `Hom(-,I)` of a degree-0-concentrated complex ⟹ zero in positive degree ⟹ transport across the quasi-iso to `Č•(U,I)`'s positive-degree homology (exact tail of `CechBridge.lean:874-911`, structurally verbatim).

**2. `ses_cech_h1` (`CechBridge.lean:659-826`, L1's surjectivity ingredient — Stacks `lemma-ses-cech-h1`).**
Proof strategy (10 lines): given SES `0→F→G→H→0` and local lifts `sLoc i ∈ G(Uᵢ)` of `s∈H(⨆Uᵢ)`, form the degree-1 cochain of pairwise differences `dGcoord σ = sLoc(σ1)|_σ - sLoc(σ0)|_σ`; show `gπ` kills it (LES exactness on sections, from `hπι`/`hker`); lift the killed cochain into `F` pointwise (`hker`); show the lift is a genuine 1-cocycle in `F` (transport the `d²=0` identity of `G`'s cochain through the mono `fι`); apply `Ȟ¹(U,F)=0` to extract a 0-cochain `t` with `dt` = the lift (`sectionCech_one_coboundary_of_isZero_homology`); correct `sLoc` by `fι(t)` to get a genuinely compatible family; glue via `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSheafUniqueGluing` on `G`; check the glued section maps to `s` by separatedness of `H`. **Port cost**: mechanical (swap `X.PresheafOfModules`/its restriction API for `𝒮`'s `sheafToPresheaf`/`forget₂`-composed presheaf and Mathlib's generic sheaf-gluing lemma), but the sheer bookkeeping volume (7 private helper lemmas, `CechBridge.lean:552-635`) means this is a **large, low-conceptual-risk, high-LOC** port item — budget ~250-350 LOC.

**3. The Čech-hom-identification `cechComplex_hom_identification`/`homCechComplexMapOpIso`/`sectionCechComplexMapOpIso` (`CechBridge.lean:121-369`).**
This is the piece with the **least direct Mathlib precedent for the new setting**, because it must reconcile two different presentations of "the Čech complex": (a) Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor`'s `FormalCoproduct`-based cosimplicial object (used to define `Scheme.cechCochain`/`Scheme.cechCohomology`, `Carriers.lean:562-578`, the target the whole port must land on) versus (b) the free-presheaf-resolution's own natural cosimplicial presentation `Hom(K(U)_•,F)` (built from `Sigma.ι`/`opCoproductIsoProduct`/`piComparison`, mirroring `homCechSectionIsoApp`, `CechBridge.lean:162-254`). The `X.Modules` proof needed this because `sectionCechComplex` was **hand-rolled** to match `K(𝒰)_•`'s shape by construction; in the port, the target complex `Scheme.cechCochain` is fixed externally by `cechComplexFunctor`, so the identification must instead show `Hom(K(U)_•, F) ≅ (cechComplexFunctor U).obj (sheafToPresheaf.obj F)` degreewise (`Hom(⊕_σ free(yoneda V_σ), F) ≅ ∏_σ F(V_σ)`, matching `FormalCoproduct.mk _ U`.cech's degree-`p` object `U.power (Fin(p+1))`), then check differential-intertwining against `FormalCoproduct`'s coface maps rather than the project's own `homOfLE`-based ones. Budget ~150-250 LOC of genuinely new work; recommend prototyping the degree-0 and degree-1 cases by hand first (`lean_multi_attempt`/`lean_goal` against `FormalCoproduct.mk`'s unfolding) before committing to the general-`n` proof, since the `FormalCoproduct`/`SimplicialObject` API's defeq behavior around `U.power`/`E.rightOp` is unfamiliar territory for this codebase (no prior project usage found).

### D.2 The 3 hardest lemmas to port

**1. `injective_cech_acyclic` (`CechBridge.lean:874`, base-case ingredient of L3/via `BasisCovSystem.injective_acyclic`).**
Proof strategy to mirror (10 lines):
1. Build the free Čech chain complex of presheaves `K(U)_p = ⨁_{σ:Fin(p+1)→ι} free(yoneda(V_σ))` (analogue: `⨁_σ (yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj V_σ`), with differential the alternating sum of face maps induced by inclusions `V_{σ} ≤ V_{σ∘δᵢ}`.
2. Show the augmentation `K(U)_• → O_U[0]` (`O_U` = "presheaf that is `⊕_{i:V_i⊇V} k`-ish structure of the cover", concretely `coverStructurePresheaf`-analogue) is a quasi-iso, via the *sectionwise* contracting homotopy: fix `i_fix` with `V ⊆ U_{i_fix}`, homotopy `h(s)_{i₀,…,iₚ} = [i₀ = i_fix]·s_{i₁,…,iₚ}`, check `dh+hd=id` (`combHomotopy_spec`/`combDifferential_exact`, `FreePresheafComplex.lean:483-580`, coefficient-agnostic, ports verbatim).
3. Show `(sheafToPresheaf J _).obj I` is injective in the presheaf category, for `I` injective in `𝒮` — **one-liner** via `Injective.injective_of_adjoint (sheafificationAdjunction J (ModuleCat k)) I`, using Mathlib's free `PreservesFiniteLimits (presheafToSheaf J A)` instance (§C.4) — this step is **much shorter** than the `X.Modules` analogue `injective_toPresheafOfModules`.
4. `Hom(-,I_pshf)` is exact (`preadditiveYoneda_obj_preservesFiniteColimits_of_injective`, `CechBridge.lean:401`, category-generic, reuse verbatim).
5. Apply `Hom(-,I_pshf)` to the quasi-iso augmentation ⟹ quasi-iso of `Hom`-complexes; identify `Hom(K(U)_•,I_pshf)` with the section Čech complex `Č•(U,I)` (analogue of `cechComplex_hom_identification`/`homCechComplexMapOpIso`) — this identification against Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor` cosimplicial object (rather than a hand-rolled one) is genuinely new plumbing (~150-250 LOC) but structurally the same shape as `CechBridge.lean:121-369`.
6. Conclude: source complex is `Hom(-,I)` of a degree-0-concentrated complex ⟹ zero in positive degree ⟹ transport across the quasi-iso to `Č•(U,I)`'s positive-degree homology (exact tail of `CechBridge.lean:874-911`, structurally verbatim).

**2. `ses_cech_h1` (`CechBridge.lean:659-826`, L1's surjectivity ingredient — Stacks `lemma-ses-cech-h1`).**
Proof strategy (10 lines): given SES `0→F→G→H→0` and local lifts `sLoc i ∈ G(Uᵢ)` of `s∈H(⨆Uᵢ)`, form the degree-1 cochain of pairwise differences `dGcoord σ = sLoc(σ1)|_σ - sLoc(σ0)|_σ`; show `gπ` kills it (LES exactness on sections, from `hπι`/`hker`); lift the killed cochain into `F` pointwise (`hker`); show the lift is a genuine 1-cocycle in `F` (transport the `d²=0` identity of `G`'s cochain through the mono `fι`); apply `Ȟ¹(U,F)=0` to extract a 0-cochain `t` with `dt` = the lift (`sectionCech_one_coboundary_of_isZero_homology`); correct `sLoc` by `fι(t)` to get a genuinely compatible family; glue via `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSheafUniqueGluing` on `G`; check the glued section maps to `s` by separatedness of `H`. **Port cost**: mechanical (swap `X.PresheafOfModules`/its restriction API for `𝒮`'s `sheafToPresheaf`/`forget₂`-composed presheaf and Mathlib's generic sheaf-gluing lemma), but the sheer bookkeeping volume (7 private helper lemmas, `CechBridge.lean:552-635`) means this is a **large, low-conceptual-risk, high-LOC** port item — budget ~250-350 LOC.

**3. The Čech-hom-identification `cechComplex_hom_identification`/`homCechComplexMapOpIso`/`sectionCechComplexMapOpIso` (`CechBridge.lean:121-369`).**
This is the piece with the **least direct Mathlib precedent for the new setting**, because it must reconcile two different presentations of "the Čech complex": (a) Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor`'s `FormalCoproduct`-based cosimplicial object (used to define `Scheme.cechCochain`/`Scheme.cechCohomology`, `Carriers.lean:562-578`, the target the whole port must land on) versus (b) the free-presheaf-resolution's own natural cosimplicial presentation `Hom(K(U)_•,F)` (built from `Sigma.ι`/`opCoproductIsoProduct`/`piComparison`, mirroring `homCechSectionIsoApp`, `CechBridge.lean:162-254`). The `X.Modules` proof needed this because `sectionCechComplex` was **hand-rolled** to match `K(𝒰)_•`'s shape by construction; in the port, the target complex `Scheme.cechCochain` is fixed externally by `cechComplexFunctor`, so the identification must instead show `Hom(K(U)_•, F) ≅ (cechComplexFunctor U).obj (sheafToPresheaf.obj F)` degreewise (`Hom(⊕_σ free(yoneda V_σ), F) ≅ ∏_σ F(V_σ)`, matching `FormalCoproduct.mk _ U`.cech's degree-`p` object `U.power (Fin(p+1))`), then check differential-intertwining against `FormalCoproduct`'s coface maps rather than the project's own `homOfLE`-based ones. Budget ~150-250 LOC of genuinely new work; recommend prototyping the degree-0 and degree-1 cases by hand first (`lean_multi_attempt`/`lean_goal` against `FormalCoproduct.mk`'s unfolding) before committing to the general-`n` proof, since the `FormalCoproduct`/`SimplicialObject` API's defeq behavior around `U.power`/`E.rightOp` is unfamiliar territory for this codebase (no prior project usage found).
